hypothesis.statement: In the CAU-10 framework (Al(OH) helical cis-corner-sharing chains), the 2,5-furandicarboxylate linker of MIL-160 places a ring oxygen next to the μ-OH that can accept a hydrogen bond from the first water held at the μ-OH. This extra acceptor contact causes stronger water binding in MIL-160, and because it must be broken on release it raises regeneration energy by the same mechanism. Replacing the ring O with S (thiophene, poor acceptor) or removing the heteroatom (benzene, CAU-10-H isophthalate parent) should remove the contact and weaken binding and regeneration cost together.
hypothesis.rationale: No measurements are on record; this is design, not evidence. This is the cheapest claim testing the campaign's central tension: assuming 'minimize water_adsorption_energy' means more negative is better, stronger dry-air binding pulls against low release heat. If one feature (a heteroatom acceptor contact in the pore) controls both, the objectives are a single trade-off axis and a later round should seek a deliberately moderate binding site rather than stack hydrophilic features. If the coupling fails (condition 3), the objectives are separable at the pocket scale, which would be the more useful finding. MIL-160 and CAU-10-H share the same Al-OH chain topology and differ only in the linker ring, the cleanest isoreticular pair among known water-harvesting MOFs; MOF-303 and MOF-801 were excluded because metal/topology differences would confound the linker comparison. A pyrrole N–H (donor, not acceptor) arm would separate 'acceptor contact' from 'any polar heteroatom'; it is included as an auxiliary fourth candidate but does not enter the kill criterion, since one point cannot carry a claim alone — a later round would need to build that comparison. Scope: pocket-scale binding/desorption energetics in a few-hundred-atom cell only; no isotherm step, capacity, cycling or hydrolytic stability, rate or device yield claimed. regeneration_energy is at best a proxy for practical release heat and will be read as such if flagged proxy. What would change my mind: furan, thiophene and benzene within 5 kJ/mol of each other in adsorption energy (pore geometry and μ-OH dominate), or adsorption and regeneration moving independently across the three arms.
hypothesis.prediction: Sign convention: water_adsorption_energy negative when exothermic; 5 kJ/mol is a chosen minimum effect size, not an estimate. (1) MIL-160's water_adsorption_energy is at least 5 kJ/mol more negative than CAU-10-H's. (2) MIL-160's water_adsorption_energy is at least 5 kJ/mol more negative than the thiophene analogue's. (3) MIL-160's regeneration_energy is at least 5 kJ/mol higher than both CAU-10-H and the thiophene analogue.
hypothesis.falsification_criterion: Refuted if any holds: (1) MIL-160's water_adsorption_energy is less than 5 kJ/mol more negative than CAU-10-H's; (2) MIL-160's water_adsorption_energy is less than 5 kJ/mol more negative than the thiophene analogue's; (3) MIL-160 binds at least 5 kJ/mol more strongly than both comparators but its regeneration_energy is not at least 5 kJ/mol above both. If the thiophene arm is flagged OOD or low-confidence, condition 2 is recorded as undecided and the verdict rests on conditions 1 and 3. If MIL-160 or CAU-10-H is flagged OOD, the round is inconclusive.

batch_plan.strategy: Four candidates, all in the CAU-10 / MIL-160 topology. Hold fixed: Al(III), the μ-OH helical cis-corner-sharing chain, carboxylate positions, topology and water loading protocol. Score every candidate for water_adsorption_energy and regeneration_energy. (1) Reference, furan: MIL-160, Al(OH)(2,5-furandicarboxylate), reported structure as retrieved. (2) Comparator, benzene: CAU-10-H, Al(OH)(isophthalate), reported structure as retrieved. (3) Comparator, thiophene: Al(OH)(2,5-thiophenedicarboxylate) in the MIL-160 framework — from MIL-160 replace the ring O with S at every linker (100%), relax the cell. (4) Auxiliary, pyrrole (not in kill criterion): Al(OH)(pyrrole-2,5-dicarboxylate) in the MIL-160 framework — from MIL-160 replace the ring O with N–H at every linker (100%), relax the cell. No partial substitutions: every linker in a candidate carries the same ring. If MIL-160 cannot be retrieved, do not substitute another MOF; report the round as unrunnable.

- No other edit to these parents informs the stated claim. Partial-linker mixtures, F-bridged variants and cation swaps would all be rejected as off-spec.

1. ADOCEC/MIL-160, as retrieved.
2. aloh225K/CAU-10-H, as retrieved.
3. MIL-160 with ring O→S (thiophene).
4. Approved: c-cm503311x_aloh225K and c-cm503311x_alf400K.

c-cm503311x_aloh225K. Its formula is listed as unknown. Its child c-h1-4 implies Al4C32 with 20 O sites, i.e. 8 C and 5 O per Al. That matches Al(OH)(isophthalate) = CAU-10-H, not MIL-160 (which would be 6 C and 6 O per Al). If the identification holds, this is the CAU-10-H arm for condition 1.
Warning: the label reads "Al(O)" and the child is H-free, which is consistent with a parent CIF lacking H positions. I cannot confirm this from the provenance. The Analyst must check that the scored structure has H on the bridging O. If it does not, treat the result as unusable for h1, not as weak binding.

c-cm503311x_alf400K. μ-F Al-chain dicarboxylate is plausible chemistry. It does not enter h1 conditions 1–3. It bears on the premise that the first water is held at μ-OH: similar binding with μ-F would weaken that premise. It is in the right family for the campaign goal.
The 400K coordinates are probably dehydrated, while the aloh entry is at 225K. Cross-comparison mixes the bridging-anion effect with temperature-dependent cell or linker differences, so differences of a few kJ/mol between them should not be attributed purely to the anion.

Batch-level problem. Neither MIL-160 nor the thiophene-dicarboxylate analogue is in the batch, and every h1 condition compares against MIL-160. h1 is therefore insufficient data. Missing measurements: MIL-160 water_adsorption_energy and regeneration_energy, and both energies for the thiophene analogue. Do not mark the round refuted, supported or inconclusive-by-OOD on this batch.
The planner should retrieve MIL-160 and an Al thiophene-dicarboxylate in the CAU-10 topology, with μ-OH hydrogens present in all three. If the thiophene analogue exists only in a different chain topology, record condition 2 as undecided per the hypothesis's own rule.

Reading water_adsorption_energy. Read it as the strongest-site, low-coverage binding energy on a few-hundred-atom cell, not as the loading-averaged isosteric heat. It is the most negative value the system will show, so treat it as a bound on binding strength. Do not convert it to an isotherm step position or an RH threshold.

Reading regeneration_energy. It is a proxy. Real regeneration cost includes desorption enthalpy integrated over loading, framework sensible heat, and kinetics over seconds to minutes, all beyond picosecond simulation. If it is just a desorption energy for one or a few waters, condition 3 nearly restates conditions 1–2, and their agreement is partly built in rather than independent support. Check its definition before claiming the mechanism is confirmed.

Expected extrapolation. Any structure missing μ-OH hydrogens is effectively outside what the method treats for this question. Al-carboxylate frameworks with water are likely near the ODAC training domain. Static or picosecond calculations miss linker rotation and cell change on hydration, so binding on a fixed dry-phase framework may misplace the water.

measurement.note:
Binding energy of ONE water molecule at 0 K, from the ODAC23 EquiformerV2 checkpoint. Negative is favourable. ACCURACY, measured against 8 published DFT reference energies for these same frameworks: MAE 0.24 eV, mean signed +0.21 eV (it tends to UNDER-bind), worst case 0.52 eV. That is a tendency and not a bound — 2 of 8 overshot and bound more strongly than the reference.
The error is BIMODAL, which the MAE hides: on 4 of 8 frameworks the placement search found a site matching the reference and agreed to within 0.015 eV, while on 3 it missed the true strong-binding site and was wrong by about 0.5 eV. The limiting factor is therefore the site search, not the energy model: this screens a few deterministic placements (16 here, 3 relaxed) against a rigid framework, where the references come from an exhaustive search with full DFT relaxation.
RANKING IS UNRELIABLE: Spearman rank correlation against the reference energies is only 0.19 over 8 frameworks. Do not treat an ordering of frameworks by this number as established without checking the per-site detail. Note also that those references are ODAC23 training data, so even this comparison is in-distribution and flatters the model. This is NOT water uptake: uptake is a loading isotherm at a given temperature and humidity, which cannot be computed from a single-molecule binding energy. OUT OF DISTRIBUTION: this framework contains no hydrogen atoms at all. Aromatic C-H and any bridging mu-OH proton are missing from the deposited structure, and a bare mu-O is a different site for water than a mu-OH, so the binding energy is for a framework that is not quite the real one.

measurement.note:
PROXY for the energy needed to regenerate the framework. What it actually is: the magnitude of the computed binding energy of a SINGLE water molecule at 0 K, sign-flipped, i.e. the work to remove that one molecule from its site. A positive value means water is bound and energy is needed to drive it off.
What it is NOT, and why it is imperfect: (1) it is not the isosteric heat of adsorption, which is what a real regeneration duty is based on; (2) it ignores how binding weakens as loading rises, so it reflects the FIRST, strongest-bound water and overestimates the per-molecule cost at working loading; (3) it excludes water-water hydrogen bonding and pore condensation, which dominate uptake in a real water harvester; (4) it omits zero-point energy and all entropic terms, so it is not a free energy at any temperature; (5) it excludes the sensible heat of heating the framework itself, which is a large part of a real regeneration budget. (6) it inherits everything wrong with the adsorption energy it is derived from, including the weak rank correlation (Spearman 0.19) against reference energies — so it is NOT a reliable way to rank frameworks either, and it is never a thermal duty.

body.reasoning: Insufficient data. All three falsification conditions compare against MIL-160's water_adsorption_energy or regeneration_energy, and MIL-160 was never measured. The thiophene analogue is also absent, so none of the conditions can be evaluated. c-cm503311x_aloh225K is only putatively CAU-10-H. That identification is the Skeptic's inference from a perturbed child's stoichiometry (8 C and 5 O per Al); the framework's own formula is recorded as unknown. Its model value is flagged OOD because the structure has no H atoms and the bridging site is a bare μ-O. The criterion's OOD clause would therefore make the round inconclusive even if MIL-160 had been measured. The verdict itself, however, rests on the missing MIL-160 data. Condition 3 is structurally redundant. regeneration_energy is the model adsorption energy sign-flipped and multiplied by 96.485 kJ/mol per eV (0.0595 eV gives 5.741 kJ/mol; 0.5071 eV gives 48.93 kJ/mol), so it can never fail independently of conditions 1–2. The 5 kJ/mol threshold (0.0518 eV) is far below the model MAE of 0.24 eV, the ~0.5 eV site-miss mode, and the Spearman ρ of 0.19. On aloh225K the model underbinds the DFT reference by 0.2837 eV; on alf400K it overbinds by 0.1022 eV. The μ-F vs μ-OH gap in the DFT references, 0.0617 eV (5.95 kJ/mol), is confounded by temperature, hydration state and missing H, so it cannot be assigned to the bridging anion. The Pareto point for aloh225K mixes a model-derived regeneration_energy with a DFT-reference adsorption energy, so its 0.600 vs 0.400 scalar ordering is not like-for-like. heuristics.text: Reject H-free CIFs at retrieval time, before scoring, whenever the hypothesis depends on a μ-OH or other H-bond donor site; a bare μ-O is a different binding site.

Do not write a falsification condition on regeneration_energy alongside one on water_adsorption_energy from the same source: the proxy is exactly -E_ads × 96.485 kJ/mol per eV. Either drop the condition or replace it with an independent measurement; if none is available, state that the regeneration half of the mechanism is untestable with current tools.

Do not decide a 5 kJ/mol (0.0518 eV) effect from model-scored adsorption energies unless each framework's placement is shown to match the reference site. Use ODAC23 DFT reference values for the decisive arms where they exist.
Treat a model-reference gap above 0.1 eV as a site-search failure: rerun with more placements, or relax more than 3 of the 16, before using that framework's model number anywhere.

Never mix a DFT-reference water_adsorption_energy with a model-derived regeneration_energy on the same Pareto point. Rebuild the frontier from a single source per candidate and record which source was used.
Require a recorded formula or a confirmed identity for each hypothesis arm before measurement; stoichiometry inferred from a perturbed child is not enough to anchor a falsification condition.

Do not compare μ-F and μ-OH frameworks from coordinate sets at different temperatures (400 K vs 225 K) to test the bridging-site premise. Retrieve both at matched hydration state, or treat few-kJ/mol differences as confounded.

This is a rerun of h1 under the standing orders. It is not a sign that the line is working. h1 was never tested: MIL-160 and the thiophene arm were never measured, and the putative CAU-10-H (c-cm503311x_aloh225K) has no recorded formula and no H atoms. hypothesis.statement: In the CAU-10 framework (helical cis-corner-sharing Al(OH) chains), the first water molecule binds more strongly in MIL-160 than in CAU-10-H. proposal.summary: No hypothesis was refuted, and none was confirmed. h1, h2 and h3 all closed inconclusive; each failed at retrieval, before any decisive number existed. Rounds 2 and 3 recorded zero measurements. The only data are 14 values on two depositions, c-cm503311x_aloh225K and c-cm503311x_alf400K, both formula unknown and with no H atoms. aloh225K's identity as CAU-10-H is inferred from a perturbed child's stoichiometry, not recorded. MIL-160 was never retrieved in any form; the thiophene analogue, alf350K and ADOCEC have no measurements. The most reliable results are negative and concern the campaign's own tools. (1) Both model water energies fail the 0.1 eV site-search line and cannot be used: aloh225K model −0.0595 eV (OOD) vs DFT reference −0.3432 eV, underbinding by 0.2837 eV; alf400K model −0.5071 eV (OOD) vs DFT −0.4049 eV, overbinding by 0.1022 eV. (2) regeneration_energy is not an independent measurement: it is exactly −E_ads(model) × 96.485 kJ/mol per eV, so the two objectives are one number with opposite optimisation directions and any single-source Pareto front is degenerate, with every candidate non-dominated. (3) The current frontier is not like-for-like: it pairs model regeneration values with DFT adsorption values (5.741 kJ/mol beside −0.3432 eV; 48.93 kJ/mol beside −0.4049 eV), and the 5.741 kJ/mol comes from a placement that missed its own reference by 0.2837 eV, so the 0.600 vs 0.400 scalar ordering is not established. Rebuilt from the DFT source alone, by unit conversion only and not as new measurements: aloh225K 0.3432 eV → 33.11 kJ/mol; alf400K 0.4049 eV → 39.07 kJ/mol. What the campaign does hold: the DFT references say alf400K (μ-F label) binds one water more strongly than aloh225K (μ-O label, H-free) by 0.0617 eV (5.95 kJ/mol) at confidence 0.55; that gap is unattributed, confounded by coordinate-set temperature (400 K vs 225 K), unknown hydration state, missing H and unknown formulas. Geometric descriptors cannot separate the two: pore diameter 7.081 Å vs 7.379 Å (difference 0.298 Å, inside the ±0.60 Å grid limit), void fraction 0.2223 vs 0.2246, surface area 237.8 vs 239.2 m²/g. What the campaign failed to establish: nothing shows either framework captures water from dry air; there is no isotherm, step position or uptake, no isosteric heat or thermal duty, and no regeneration measurement independent of the binding energy. Neither candidate should be called a low-heat water harvester. Recommendation: c-cm503311x_aloh225K is the lab target, not as a harvester, but as the only measured candidate whose putative identity, Al(OH)(isophthalate), CAU-10-H, AlC8H5O5 per Al, is a synthesisable compound with a μ-OH site; its DFT first-water binding of −0.3432 eV is the weaker of the two measured. c-cm503311x_alf400K is the comparison arm only if its linker and fluoride bridge are confirmed; its linker is currently unrecorded.
synthesis_route: Note: steps 1–6 target CAU-10-H, the putative identity of aloh225K. Reaction quantities are commonly used solvothermal CAU-10-H conditions and must be checked against the primary report before use; they are procedure, not campaign measurements.

0. Gate — confirm identities before synthesis: obtain the cm503311x deposition CIFs and associated publication; record for aloh225K and alf400K the linker, bridging anion, formula per Al and guest/coordinated-water content. If aloh225K is not Al(OH)(benzene-1,3-dicarboxylate), stop: the route makes the wrong compound. If alf400K's linker is not isophthalate, it is not a matched arm and step 7 does not apply.
1. Weigh Al2(SO4)3·18H2O, 0.80 g (1.2 mmol), and isophthalic acid (benzene-1,3-dicarboxylic acid), 0.20 g (1.2 mmol), into the PTFE liner of a steel autoclave.
2. Add 2.4 mL deionised water and 0.6 mL N,N-dimethylformamide; seal the autoclave.
3. Heat in a convection oven at 135 °C for 12 h, then cool to room temperature in the oven.

4. Recover the solid by vacuum filtration; wash three times with deionised water and three times with ethanol; dry in air at 100 °C. Check FTIR for a free carboxylic-acid C=O band from unreacted linker; if present, re-suspend in ethanol under reflux and repeat until absent.
5. Repeat steps 1–4 until at least 0.5 g is collected (enough for isotherms at three temperatures plus TGA-DSC and cycling). Take PXRD on each batch and pool only batches whose patterns match.

6. Activate at 150 °C under dynamic vacuum (below 10⁻² mbar) for 12 h immediately before every sorption measurement; confirm by TGA that the activated mass sits on a plateau below decomposition onset.

7. μ-F comparison arm (conditional): only if step 0 confirms alf400K as Al(F)(isophthalate), reproduce the fluoride route in the deposition's own publication verbatim, without improvising fluoride source or ratio; activate as in step 6.
validation_protocol: V1 Identity and purity: PXRD (Cu Kα, 5–50° 2θ) with Pawley fit against the deposited CIF cell; CHN combustion analysis; Al by ICP-OES after acid digestion; F by ion chromatography or fluoride ion-selective electrode after digestion; TGA in air to constant residue (theoretical for AlC8H5O5 from stoichiometry: C 46.17 wt%, H 2.42 wt%, Al2O3 residue 24.50 wt%); solid-state ¹H MAS NMR and FTIR to show the μ-OH proton; ¹⁹F MAS NMR to show the μ-F bridge on the step 7 arm. Establishes the formula and H status the campaign never had.

V2 Water vapour isotherms: adsorption and desorption at 15, 25 and 35 °C, P/P0 0.02–0.90, by volumetric vapour analyser or gravimetric DVS. Outputs step position, uptake (g/g) and hysteresis — the first data on whether either material captures water at low RH.

V3 Isosteric heat versus loading from V2 by Clausius–Clapeyron on a virial or spline fit. Low-loading limit tests the DFT first-water ordering; value at working loading is the regeneration-relevant quantity the proxy could not provide; independent of the adsorption-energy proxy.

V4 Calvet microcalorimetry: dose water onto activated sample at the lowest accessible loading to obtain a direct differential enthalpy for the first water, cross-checking V3 at low coverage where Clausius–Clapeyron is least reliable.

V5 TGA-DSC regeneration: equilibrate at 25 °C and 30% RH, ramp 2 K/min to 150 °C under dry N2; record desorption onset, temperature at 90% water mass loss, and integrated endotherm per gram of water released; run a dry activated sample through the same programme and subtract to separate sensible heat. Lab-scale regeneration measurement independent of V3.
V6 Cycling: 20 adsorption–desorption cycles (25 °C/30% RH to 150 °C), then PXRD and a repeat 25 °C isotherm. Addresses stability, which the models cannot.

V7 CO2 isotherm at 25 °C: in both DFT references single CO2 binds more strongly than single water (alf400K −0.6703 vs −0.4049 eV; aloh225K −0.5714 vs −0.3432 eV), so competitive uptake from air must be measured, not inferred from 0 K single-molecule energies.
